design_rationale: The four schools were purposively selected, and although two schools were described as 'randomly sampled' to form the intervention group, the paper does not explicitly report random allocation of schools or participants to conditions; under the specified rule, unclear assignment is classified as non-randomized.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intervention assignment occurred at the school level without clearly reported random allocation or adequate control for school- and participant-level confounding, and the groups differed at baseline in itching while most outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted post-intervention comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four elementary schools in Seoul, Korea, were selected via purposive sampling to participate in the study; participants from two schools (randomly sampled) formed the test group whereas participants from the remaining two schools formed the comparison, or control group.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants self-selected after school-level condition assignment, and post-enrollment exclusions and withdrawals differed by group and included reasons plausibly related to intervention response and outcome measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were recruited by placing posters in the subject schools. Additional recruitment occurred through written contact with parents of children found to have AD.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention and control conditions were defined by school before outcomes were assessed, and the SACP content and delivery were described clearly, making intervention misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants from two schools (randomly sampled) formed the test group whereas participants from the remaining two schools formed the comparison, or control group.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and providers necessarily knew intervention status, delivery intensity varied across participants, and the analysis excluded withdrawals rather than following an intention-to-treat principle, although no specific contamination or co-intervention was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Case management was provided by a health teacher through face-to-face interviews (one to six sessions) and phone interviews (two to five sessions) with parents.

domain_judgments.rationale: Twenty-three of 121 enrolled dyads were excluded from analysis, including 15 consent withdrawals with group-specific and outcome-related reasons, and no sensitivity analysis or method addressing missing outcomes was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A further 15 dyads (4 test groups; 11 control groups) withdrew their consent and were also excluded.

domain_judgments.rationale: Most outcomes, including the nominally objective severity assessment, were reported by parents who knew whether they received the educational program, and intervention parents were specifically trained in severity measurement, creating differential measurement risk.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The OAS assessment was carried out by parents in the home setting. Parents were also provided with one-on-one education on “measuring methods for atopic dermatitis severity” by a health teacher during part 2 of the intervention (Case Management).

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified analysis plan was reported, numerous outcomes and time-point comparisons were tested with several statistical methods, and the abstract emphasizes a parental-efficacy finding that arose from a within-intervention-group follow-up comparison despite a null between-group post-test result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To examine differences in pre-, post- and follow-up testing of the test group, the respective variables were analyzed using paired t test, Friedman test.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven by uncontrolled confounding and participant self-selection, differential attrition with complete-case analysis, unblinded parent-reported outcome measurement, and substantial scope for selective analysis/reporting. Clear intervention classification does not offset these serious risks.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports that a random number generator assigned 61 pediatric patients to the intervention or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although sequence generation was explicitly random and observed baseline SCORAD scores were reasonably similar, allocation concealment was not described and some baseline differences appeared in age-specific quality-of-life scores.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A random number generator was used to place the participants into either the intervention group or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they attended the workshop, and the report does not describe blinding, contamination, adherence by randomized group, or a clear intention-to-treat analysis, although the intervention was added to usual management and prescribed treatment was not intended to change.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The interventional group undertook the education program through a 2-hour workshop, together with their normal management regimen. The control group received the usual care including routine education, medical consultation, and management.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 3 of 61 randomized participants were lost to follow-up, so outcome data were available for approximately 95% of participants and the stated reason for loss was unlikely to depend on outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three participants were lost to follow-up at week 4 and week 12 (change of address and unable to contact them) but their data were included in the analysis at baseline and as missing values at week 4 and week 12.

domain_judgments.rationale: SCORAD, the primary outcome supporting the main conclusion, contains subjective components and the report does not state that clinical assessors were blinded; knowledge of assignment could therefore plausibly influence assessments, while self-reported quality-of-life and family outcomes were also completed by unblinded participants or parents.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the week 4 and week 12 visits, both groups were assessed by using the clinical SCORAD assessment tool to determine the severity of their eczema, the QOL (either CDQOL or IDQOL depending on age of participant) and DFI questionnaires were repeated on both the control and the experimental groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and several outcomes, time points, age-specific instruments, and analyses were available, creating scope for selective reporting despite presentation of the main measured outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ANCOVA was performed to identify differences between the intervention group and the control group at each data collection time (baseline, week 4, week 12) for each outcome variable.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the primary SCORAD outcome could have been influenced by unblinded assessment in this overt educational intervention. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, unclear handling of deviations, and absence of a preregistered analysis plan, although attrition was minimal.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that participants were divided into intervention and control groups using random number generation.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random-number sequence was used and most baseline measures were balanced, but allocation concealment was not described and significant baseline imbalances occurred in stress and both anxiety measures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: participants were divided using the method of random number generation into two groups: intervention and control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received education, the control group sought significantly more outside education, and the analysis appears to include only completers rather than an intention-to-treat population.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: the control group educated itself more between the visits.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 6 of 134 randomized participants withdrew (4.5%), with equal analyzed group sizes, so outcome data were available for nearly all participants and substantial bias from missingness is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Six participants withdrew from the study; so the study was completed by 64 participants in the intervention and 64 in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although validated outcome instruments were used consistently, most outcomes were parent-reported and parents knew their assignment, while blinding of the physician assessing SCORAD was not reported, making differential measurement plausible for this subjective behavioral intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the second visit, the physician-assessed the severity of the disease using SCORAD index... and again completed the following questionnaires: PO SCORAD, PSS, STAI and FDLQI.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcomes and subscales were tested, leaving scope for selective choice of measurements or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the change in the severity of eczema assessed using SCORAD and PO SCORAD index and changes of symptom scores for pruritus and sleeplessness. Secondary outcome measures included changes of stress level according to the PSS, changes of anxiety level according to STAI and changes of parental quality of life scores according to the Croatian version of the FDLQI.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by the high risk in outcome measurement because unblinded parents reported most subjective outcomes and physician blinding was not reported. Additional concerns arise from unclear allocation concealment, baseline psychological imbalances, control-group contamination, completer analysis, and lack of preregistration.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were allocated 1:1 using a simple, nonstratified randomization scheme generated from randomization tables.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation was explicitly based on randomization tables and measured baseline characteristics were broadly balanced, but allocation concealment was not described and the unequal group sizes are unexplained under the stated 1:1 scheme.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants were randomized in a 1:1 simple, nonstratified randomization scheme generated using randomization tables.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trainers were necessarily aware of assignment, individualized therapy and diet were unrestricted, and the paper does not clearly report an intention-to-treat analysis or whether co-interventions and deviations differed between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients received therapy and diet recommendations based on their individual disease severity, with no restrictions in the study protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up completeness and attrition are not transparently reported, while the emollient questionnaire analysis includes only 430 of 542 randomized participants and quality-of-life denominators are substantially smaller, with no reasons for missingness or sensitivity analyses to show that results were unbiased.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intervention group(n = 235) ... Control group(n = 195)

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open label and investigators were not blinded; the primary SCORAD measure includes assessor-dependent clinical ratings that could be influenced by assignment knowledge, while quality-of-life and knowledge outcomes were also susceptible to participant or parent awareness and the knowledge questionnaire was unvalidated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The third limitation is that the investigators were not blinded during the study, which may have influenced the results.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and several outcomes, time points, age-specific instruments, questionnaire items, and change-versus-follow-up analyses permit selective reporting, although the principal tabulated outcomes are presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children were assessed at baseline and after 3 and 6 months.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by inadequately characterized missing outcome data and likely bias in outcome measurement in an open-label trial with unblinded investigators. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, unrestricted co-interventions without a clearly stated intention-to-treat approach, and no reported preregistration or analysis plan.
